title: Does the Model Use the Feature? Separating Steering from Mechanism in LLMs
summary: Proposes an empirical contract to separate activation steering from actual internal model mechanisms across natural inputs.
implication: Internal model monitors and steering interventions cannot assume correlation implies causation without natural range installation and removal tests.

title: A-SAW: The Agentic Software Architecture Workflow
summary: Evaluates persistent agentic drafting for architecture-as-code under mandatory review gates, showing +19 median quality gain while finding practitioner consensus against unreviewed agent commits.
implication: Supports governance standards requiring explicit review gates on structural system descriptions; agents drafting architectural specifications must be bounded by typed catalogs and verifiable reviews.

title: Web$hell: A Unified Interface for Agentic Web Access
summary: Proposes Web$hell and WebContract to unify agentic web access under addressable information and action schemas, reducing execution cost across long-horizon web navigation and research.
implication: Directly informs agent web interaction standards: defining shared contracts for addressable DOM elements and actions allows deterministic checking of web agent requests without unstructured scraping.

title: Agent4Spec: An LLM-based Agentic System to Optimize API Specifications through Automated Validation and Market Analysis
summary: Presents Agent4Spec, an autonomous multi-agent framework that continuously detects and self-corrects OpenAPI syntax errors and identifies functional specification gaps.
implication: Interface and contract validation pipelines should adopt automated OpenAPI syntax checking and schema self-correction to maintain robust integration boundaries.

title: The Limits of Query Monitoring against Distributed Model Extraction
summary: Demonstrates that query-only monitors fail to detect distributed model extraction when colluder share is below 2.5% or when campaigns ramp slowly or relay requests.
implication: Relying exclusively on query monitoring to detect colluding actors or distributed extraction is unsafe, requiring defense-in-depth and architectural containment boundaries.

title: Why LLM Agents Collapse Without Oversight: The Enforcement Gap as the Mechanism Behind Emergence World Failures
summary: Wang demonstrates that autonomous agent collapses stem from an enforcement gap where controllers ignore safety audit flags, proving detection without binding execution control is formally irrelevant.
implication: Validates the requirement for deterministic host-enforced gates over agent execution: runtime controllers cannot delegate execution gating to advisory model reflection or self-critique.

title: Diversity Collapse in Multi-Agent LLM Systems: Structural Coupling and Collective Failure in Open-Ended Idea Generation
summary: Chen et al. show multi-agent LLM systems suffer diversity collapse and premature convergence from structural coupling, where dense interaction and status hierarchies suppress distinct ideas.
implication: Directly challenges naive multi-agent deliberation and social simulation (Research Agenda 03): dense LLM agent interactions artificially contract solution diversity, requiring explicit decoupling protocols.

title: TabReliBench: Evaluating Tabular Foundation Models Beyond Predictive Accuracy
summary: Evaluating predictive models beyond raw accuracy reveals that favorable marginal coverage fails to guarantee conditional calibration, requiring multidimensional reliability metrics across subgroups.
implication: Model evaluations and forecasting benchmarks should require subgroup calibration checks rather than relying on aggregate ranking tables that mask local failure modes.

title: RESCUE: Is This Alarm Worth Acting On? Counterfactual Evaluation of VLA Runtime Monitors
summary: Counterfactual evaluation of runtime failure monitors demonstrates that detection accuracy does not imply operational recovery, as modest false-alarm rates erase the net benefit of intervention.
implication: Agent execution guardrails and runtime oversight monitors must evaluate end-to-end intervention cost rather than standalone detection precision to prevent costly disruptive resets.

title: COPEX: Benchmarking LLM Robustness to Adversarial Context Across Model Context Protocol Layers
summary: Introduces COPEX, benchmarking model robustness to adversarial context across Model Context Protocol layers. Finds an average attack success rate of 64.4% across 3,375 trials, demonstrating vulnerabilities across client and transport layers.
implication: Shows that securing model context protocol interactions requires multi-layer defenses spanning transport, client, and tool-output filtering rather than relying on model robustness alone.

title: Quality, Not Just Outcome: A Structural Scoring Framework for Selecting Coding-Agent Trajectories for Supervised Fine-Tuning
summary: Proposes Trajectory Quality Score (TQS), a linear-time structural framework evaluating coding-agent trajectories without model-based judges. Filters repetitive inspection and tool thrashing to improve fine-tuning efficiency.
implication: Demonstrates that deterministic structural metrics on agent tool usage and trajectory dynamics can evaluate agent efficiency and detect pathological interaction loops without language model judges.

title: Non-Bayesian Social Learning with Heterogeneous and Time-Varying Aggregation Rules
summary: Generalizes Non-Bayesian social learning on connected networks, proving agent beliefs converge almost surely to ground truth even under heterogeneous, time-varying aggregation functions like DeGroot and CES rules.
implication: Enables robust decentralized belief aggregation in collective intelligence networks where individual agents adapt their aggregation heuristics over time.

title: Matched-Context Group Policy Optimization for LLM Agent Training
summary: Matched-Context Group Policy Optimization improves credit assignment in long-horizon agent rollouts by pairing actions sharing local context rather than contrasting across disparate execution branches.
implication: Agent training in simulations can isolate credit for intermediate decisions without sparse terminal feedback distorting local safety choices.

title: MENTOR: Learning from Failure with On-Policy Pedagogical Intervention
summary: MENTOR addresses zero-reward collapse in verifiable reward training through on-policy pedagogical intervention, providing intermediate hints when task difficulty causes learning signals to vanish.
implication: Autonomous training loops can recover from exploration plateaus via graded feedback rather than requiring human intervention or ungrounded rewards.

title: Constructing Pareto Frontiers of Optimal Reasoning Termination Methods for Overthinking in Reasoning Models
summary: Researchers construct Pareto frontiers of reasoning termination methods to evaluate overthinking, showing where additional test-time computation degrades reasoning accuracy instead of improving it.
implication: Bounded computation contracts require explicit early termination criteria to prevent runaway token expenditure and degraded accuracy.

title: Collective Autonomous Vehicle Routing Needs Social Awareness for Coexistence with Human Drivers
summary: Collective autonomous vehicle routing produces negative externalities for human drivers when selfish route choices minimize agent travel time at the expense of community congestion.
implication: Autonomous optimization without social coordination mechanisms degrades shared physical infrastructure, reinforcing the need for multi-stakeholder value feedback.

title: JANUS: Enhancing Long-Horizon Autonomous Research with Co-Evolving World Models
summary: JANUS enhances long-horizon autonomous research by co-evolving world models alongside worker agents, replacing reactive trial-and-error with predictive simulation of candidate actions.
implication: Autonomous discovery pipelines benefit from simulating consequences within predictive world models before committing actions to the physical environment.

title: Which Preferences to Train On? End-to-End Multi-Objective Alignment with an Adversarial Preference Distribution
summary: MAESTRO aligns models across conflicting objectives by updating an adversarial Dirichlet preference distribution via online mirror descent toward the preferences the current policy serves worst.
implication: Multi-dimensional value trade-offs can be balanced within a single policy without collapsing plural human preferences into a scalar utility function.

title: Can Language Models Learn When to Abstain? Policy Learning and Calibrated Answer Selection
summary: Evaluates whether models can learn when to abstain rather than guess; while learned selectors improve utility on TriviaQA, on NQ-Open selecting answers still performs worse than always abstaining.
implication: Demonstrates that reliable self-abstention across changing datasets remains unsolved for language models, reinforcing the need for external verifiers and deterministic runtime checks.

title: When VLMs Destroy What They Know: Spatial Representations Fall Below Lexical Priors
summary: Introduces CASP-VL and shows vision-language models systematically fail to preserve relational spatial structures when aggregating sentences into global representations, invisible to surface outputs.
implication: Shows representation-level degradation during token aggregation, meaning multi-modal models lose structural relational groundings despite appearing superficially competent on benchmarks.

title: Cooperation conflicts with equality when allocating public goods
summary: Mathematical proof showing that allocation policies designed to maximize public goods cooperation often concentrate resources among central hubs, whereas uniform equality can suppress incentives to contribute.
implication: Decentralized value allocation mechanisms must explicitly model the trade-off between maximizing collective participation and preventing structural resource concentration in network hubs.

title: PRIME: Pre-Retrieval Index Modeling Enhancement for Structured Document Retrieval-Real
summary: Shows that deterministic metadata synthesis and hierarchical retrieval structure reduce index vectors by 22.4x while matching retrieval accuracy over structured documents.
implication: Knowledge consolidation catalogs and indexes benefit from deterministic structural metadata anchors rather than unconstrained dense vector embeddings alone.

title: The Unfireable Safety Kernel: Execution-Time AI Alignment for AI Agents and Other Escapable AI Systems
summary: Presents the Unfireable Safety Kernel, formalizing four properties for runtime agent mediation outside the agent address space: process separation, pre-action enforcement, fail-closed mechanics, and signed external evidence.
implication: Validates the default-deny agent runtime broker and gatekeeper architecture: runtime controls inside the agent's address space can be bypassed, requiring an out-of-process fail-closed enforcement layer.

title: Fluid Notarization: Verifiable Evolution of Concurrently Edited Structured Documents
summary: Fluid Notarization couples JSON-native delta conflict-free replicated data types with cryptographic anchoring, proving document evolution graphs rather than snapshot states while keeping synchronization off-chain.
implication: Demonstrates that local-first personal data stores can combine deterministic off-chain conflict resolution with independently auditable cryptographic tamper evidence.
